successCriteria.description: The AuditLog entity and IAuditRepository interface are defined in the audit model file, with the action field typed as the existing AuditAction enum imported from shared/types (not redefined locally).

The AuditRepository implements IAuditRepository and its create method persists a row into the audit_log table using parameterized SQL with RETURNING *, then returns the mapped AuditLog entity (including the database-generated id).

findByEntity returns all audit records matching a given (entityType, entityId) pair, and findByPerformer returns all records matching a given performedBy; both return an empty array (not null) when no rows match.

The repository's row mapping converts snake_case database columns (entity_type, entity_id, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at) to the camelCase AuditLog fields, and preserves null oldValues/newValues as null rather than undefined.
The barrel export re-exports AuditLog, IAuditRepository, and AuditRepository so consumers import only through the module's public entry point (index.ts), matching the established module convention.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/audit/ cover all three repository methods (findByEntity, findByPerformer, create) including the empty-result and null oldValues/newValues cases, mocking pool.query from shared/db/connection.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository layer (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the audit module must not expose raw pool access or inline SQL outside AuditRepository.
No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards/casts instead (no-any rule, high severity); strict TypeScript with strict null checks must pass.
All SQL must use parameterized queries ($1, $2, …) — no string-interpolated values — to prevent SQL injection.
Modules import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); the audit module must import AuditAction from shared/types, not from a sibling module's internals.
outOfScope: AuditService, IAuditService, controller, and routes for the audit module — these are not part of this phase (only model, repository, barrel, and unit tests).
Wiring the AuditRepository into the LeaveService or any other consumer — integration of audit recording into leave workflows happens in Phase 9, not here.
Database migrations or schema creation for the audit_log table — the table schema is already defined in the reconciled architecture; this phase only implements the repository against it.

entityInvariants.invariant: An AuditLog record is immutable once created — there is no update or delete operation on the repository; it is an append-only compliance trail (GP-002). The entity does not extend BaseEntity and carries no createdAt/updatedAt; its sole timestamp is performedAt, supplied by the caller at creation time.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IAuditRepository.create(data: Omit<AuditLog, 'id'>) — persists a new audit record and returns it with the database-generated id.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Must propagate database errors (e.g., FK violation on performed_by) rather than swallowing them; the caller supplies performedAt so the repository does not default it.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IAuditRepository.findByEntity(entityType, entityId) — returns all audit records for a given entity, ordered to support chronological review.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an empty array when no rows match; never returns null.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IAuditRepository.findByPerformer(performedBy) — returns all audit records performed by a given actor.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an empty array when no rows match; never returns null.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The action field must use the existing AuditAction enum (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT) imported from shared/types — it must not be redefined or duplicated in the audit module.
The repository must obtain its database connection by importing the existing `pool` export from shared/db/connection, the same source every other repository uses — no separate Pool instantiation.

The repository must follow the established repository pattern: a class implementing the interface, parameterized SQL with RETURNING *, and a private mapRow helper converting snake_case columns to camelCase entity fields — matching the notification and employee repository conventions.

Unit tests must follow the established test convention: jest.mock('shared/db/connection', () => ({ pool: { query: jest.fn() } })), a makeRow helper producing snake_case rows, and assertions on both the SQL string and the mapped entity fields.

integrationPoints.why: The audit module depends on the Phase 1 AuditAction enum for the action field type; this is the sole cross-module dependency for this phase.
The AuditRepository obtains its pg Pool from the shared database connection, consistent with all other repositories.

The audit module's public IAuditRepository interface is the integration surface that the future LeaveService will consume to record audit entries for every state-changing operation (GP-002); this phase establishes that contract.
